idiom_name: dict keyed by (type(a), type(b)) with issubclass resolution cached by functools.lru_cache
implementation_notes: Python dispatches every call dynamically but only on the receiver, and functools.singledispatch covers exactly one argument, so the idiomatic replacement for the classic structure is a registry keyed by the pair of dynamic types plus an MRO/subclass walk cached with functools.lru_cache - a multimethod without the accept/visit plumbing. singledispatch and singledispatchmethod stay the right tools when only one axis varies, and third-party multiple-dispatch libraries (multipledispatch, plum, ovld) offer the same model with ambiguity diagnostics and per-signature caching if the dependency is acceptable.
pitfalls: The cache is keyed by classes and holds them strongly: per-request or dynamically created types grow it without bound - use a bounded lru_cache or a WeakKeyDictionary.
issubclass resolution depends on registration order, so a handler registered for (object, object) quietly wins if it is inserted first.
type(a) misses conversion protocols (__add__/__radd__): for operators, implement the reflected method instead of dispatching on types.

variants.name: accept(visitor) + visit_<type> protocol
variants.implementation_notes: The classic structure in duck-typed form: elements expose accept(visitor) and call visitor.visit_<concrete type>(self), so the first dispatch is an ordinary dynamic attribute lookup and the second is the visitor's own method. Nothing is checked - any object with the right methods works, and a missing method is an AttributeError at traversal time - so coverage lives in tests rather than in the type system. Use it when the element hierarchy is stable and operations group naturally into stateful visitor objects; singledispatch can drive the second dispatch by argument type when the first axis has a single receiver.
pitfalls: Nothing checks that a visitor implements every visit_* method: the omission surfaces as AttributeError on the first traversal of that pair.
Storing results in visitor attributes makes recursive traversal order-dependent and the visitor non-reentrant.
Ducks are not declared: a typo in a visit_* name is only detected when that pair is exercised.
